title: ansible Actuator input (v9)
description: Input Contract for the ansible Actuator (charter §2.3). Hand-written — derivation ladder rung 1 (§2.2). v9 (ADR-0156 D4) adds `connection.kubeconfigRef`, the REACH CREDENTIAL for an OBSERVED kubectl transport. ADR-0156's transport table recorded kubectl's requirement as "nothing" because it asked only what the GUEST needs — true, and it misses the other half: the execution pod is spawned with AutomountServiceAccountToken false ("the pod has no cluster identity"), so `kubectl exec` has no credential to reach the API server with. That is deliberate — an execution pod running arbitrary automation content must not carry ambient cluster authority — so the credential arrives brokered and use-granted like every other (§2.5), never as an ambient token. Without it a Run does not refuse: it is denied by the API server and ansible reports `unreachable … did not have permissions on the target directory`, blaming the guest for a control-node failure (§1.8). A SIBLING of v8, not a replacement: the loader takes the highest version as live, and every v8 declaration renders identically here — the field is optional and additive.

play.description: Play file content: a YAML sequence of plays (validated as YAML at Prepare). Mutually exclusive with scm and playbook. KEPT, not deprecated (ADR-0134 D4): a seven-line guard play is clearer inline than as a file in a directory. The rule is — if it is Ansible anyone would maintain, it is a file, so use `playbook`.

playbook.description: Playbook path WITHIN the project tree this Step's Actuator declares (`contentDir`, ADR-0134 D2), which the spine mounts at project/ in the EE pod. Mutually exclusive with play and scm — the three are the three content sources, and a merge between them would need a winner. The path is segment-bounded rather than lookahead-guarded: every segment must begin with an alphanumeric or underscore, so `..` is unrepresentable and the path can never leave the mounted tree. Core never reads the FILE — the estate load checks only that it exists (ADR-0117 D6: core never parses play content); the shim runs it out of project/, reusing the branch params.scm already has after its clone.

scm.description: SCM content-ref: clone a repo in the EE pod and run a playbook from it. The clone execs git inside the EE image (GPL boundary, §3); the control plane never fetches content.

repo.description: Clone URL (https:// or ssh://). Private-repo credentials arrive via the Step's credentialRefs, never here (§2.5).

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit to check out. Empty means the repo default branch.

playbook.description: Playbook path within the repo (e.g. site.yml or playbooks/deploy.yml).

extraVars.description: Extra variables passed to ansible-runner as --extra-vars (written to the runner's env/extravars). The landing field for AWX launch extra_vars and survey answers (§5.6). Never carries secret material (§2.5); credentials stay on credentialRefs. CONNECTION KEYS ARE REFUSED HERE (ADR-0126 D1): ansible_user, ansible_ssh_private_key_file and ansible_ssh_common_args are rendered by the shim from `connection`, which binds them to the CredentialRef the Step is actually authorized to use. Declaring one here is a Contract error naming the offending key.

propertyNames.$comment: ADR-0126 D1 — these belong in `connection`; see this field's description.

connection.description: How to reach the targets (ADR-0126). The ADDRESS is never here — it is the mgmt.address Facet core resolves into the typed Target coordinate (ADR-0084 D1/D2). This block is the AUTHENTICATION half of that split, exactly as AWX splits inventory-host from machine-credential. The shim renders every ansible key; core authors none (§1.4).

type.description: Connection plugin the shim renders as ansible_connection (ADR-0153 D1). CLOSED and short on purpose. `ssh` is the default and the shape every prior version assumed. `network_cli` and `netconf` are the ansible.netcommon family — the reach an enterprise network fleet needs — and both require networkOS below. winrm/psrp are ABSENT: there is no verifiable Windows target in CI, so shipping the value would ship a code path nothing has executed, and an enum that accepts it fails on a migrated fleet rather than at estate load. httpapi is absent for its own reason — it needs use_ssl/validate_certs/port knobs, and there is no defensible default for validate_certs (false is a posture nobody chose; true breaks every self-signed appliance). `local` is absent because it is a property of the TARGET, not of this Step: mgmt.address's reserved value renders ansible_connection=local per host, and a second home for that fact would be resolved by ansible's host-vars-beat-group-vars rule — implicit precedence §2.4 refuses. The shim REFUSES a non-ssh type on a run whose targets include a local one, naming both.

networkOS.description: The ansible_network_os the netcommon connection plugins require (e.g. cisco.ios.ios, arista.eos.eos, frr.frr.frr). REQUIRED when type is network_cli or netconf and REFUSED otherwise (ADR-0153 D2). Required rather than defaulted because there is nothing to infer it from, and a wrong guess CONNECTS and then issues another vendor's command syntax — a failure that points at the play. It is a per-RUN value: connection vars are inventory group vars, so a mixed-vendor View must be split into per-vendor Views rather than have the shim pick, which is the same constraint and the same resolution as the bastion chain (jumpChainOf). A per-host network.os Facet was declined for now: nothing demands it (§1.1) and mgmt.address is closed against becoming a device ontology (§9).

passwordRef.description: The login/device password, as a CredentialRef ALREADY on this Step's credentialRefs — no second credential channel is opened and the existing per-name use-check at dispatch stays the single authorization path (§2.5, ADR-0009/0052). The shim passes its MOUNT PATH as --connection-password-file: the password is never a value in the inventory, in extraVars, or in argv. That is the whole design (ADR-0153 D3) — group vars are written to inventory/hosts at 0644 beside ansible-runner's artifacts/, so a literal password there would be secret material in a Run artifact. Unlike a private KEY the mount is used in place and never staged: ansible applies no permission check to a password file, and a second copy of a secret is a second place it can leak from.

credentialRef.description: Name of a file-injecting CredentialRef on this Step.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several. Identical rule to vault.file and connection.file.

user.description: Login user; the shim renders ansible_user. Pattern-bounded — it reaches an ssh command line.

credentialRef.description: Name of a CredentialRef ALREADY on this Step's credentialRefs — no second credential channel is opened, and the existing per-name use-check at dispatch stays the single authorization path (§2.5, ADR-0009/0052). The shim renders ansible_ssh_private_key_file pointing at its mount.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several. Identical rule to vault.file.

hostKeyChecking.description: SSH host-key policy (ADR-0126 D2). Defaults to accept-new: it accepts a first key — which a just-provisioned host necessarily needs — and REFUSES a changed one, the property that actually matters. `strict` requires a pre-seeded known-hosts and fails first contact. `off` disables verification and must be written down to be used, instead of hiding inside a copy-pasted flag string. NOTE the honest limit: the accepted key is remembered for the RUN only; cross-Run memory is the booked follow-up (host key as a Facet + drift Finding).

jump.description: Per-hop AUTH for the reached-via chain (ADR-0126 D3), nearest hop first. The chain's TOPOLOGY is graph data — reached-via Relations to bastion Entities, each carrying its own mgmt.address — so no address appears here: a copy would be a second home for a fact the graph already holds (§2.4). One entry per hop; a SHORTER array reuses its last entry for the remaining hops, which is the common 'same jump credential throughout' case declared once. An EMPTY array is legitimate (an agent-forwarded or certificate-based bastion needs no per-hop auth).

credentialRef.description: A CredentialRef already on this Step — the bastion's key. credentialRefs is a list, so a second credential needs no new channel and the existing per-name use-check gates it exactly as it gates the target's (§2.5).

kubeconfigRef.description: The kubeconfig the CONTROL NODE authenticates to the Kubernetes API with, as a CredentialRef ALREADY on this Step's credentialRefs — no second credential channel, and the existing per-name use-check at dispatch stays the single authorization path (§2.5, ADR-0009/0052). Required whenever any target carries an observed `mgmt.transport` of kind `kubectl`; the shim refuses the Run by name if it is absent, rather than letting it fail as an unreachable host. The shim renders its MOUNT PATH as the `ansible_kubectl_kubeconfig` GROUP var — one Step brokers one kubeconfig, and it is the control node's credential rather than any single target's. Unlike a private KEY it is used in place and never staged: kubectl applies no permission check to a kubeconfig, and a second copy of a bearer credential on disk is a second place it can leak from. Scope it narrowly — `pods/exec` in the namespace the hosts live in is the whole grant this needs.

credentialRef.description: Name of a file-injecting CredentialRef on this Step.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several. Identical rule to vault.file and connection.file.

become.description: Privilege escalation (ADR-0117 D1). Typed — not a flag string — so escalation is a declared, reviewable value in Git and a recorded value on the Run, and so a future content-blind Control can gate it (via a declared changeClass, never by the PDP reading this field). v8 adds passwordRef (ADR-0153 D5, closing ANS-010): a password-prompting escalation target could not escalate at all before it. A passwordRef WITHOUT enabled:true is refused by the shim — supplying an escalation password for an escalation nobody requested means one of the two is a mistake, and guessing which yields either a pointless credential mount or a run that quietly does not escalate.

user.description: Escalate to this user (--become-user). Pattern-bounded: the value is rendered as an argv element, never concatenated into a command string.

method.description: Escalation method (--become-method). Enumerated: an open string here would be an injection seam.

passwordRef.description: The privilege-escalation password, as a CredentialRef ALREADY on this Step's credentialRefs — no second credential channel is opened and the existing per-name use-check at dispatch stays the single authorization path (§2.5, ADR-0009/0052). The shim passes its MOUNT PATH as --become-password-file: the password is never a value in the inventory, in extraVars, or in argv. That is the whole design (ADR-0153 D3) — group vars are written to inventory/hosts at 0644 beside ansible-runner's artifacts/, so a literal password there would be secret material in a Run artifact. Unlike a private KEY the mount is used in place and never staged: ansible applies no permission check to a password file, and a second copy of a secret is a second place it can leak from.

credentialRef.description: Name of a file-injecting CredentialRef on this Step.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several. Identical rule to vault.file and connection.file.

limit.description: Host-subset pattern (--limit). Narrows the core-resolved target set; it can never widen it — the inventory the shim renders is the View's resolved set (ADR-0051 MF4, the confused-deputy gate). Shell metacharacters are rejected.

tags.description: Only run tasks with these tags (--tags). Each element is rendered as its own argv value.

forks.description: Parallel host connections (--forks). Bounded so a Step cannot exhaust the execution pod.

diff.description: Show per-task changes (--diff) on an APPLYING run — 'converge, and show me what changed'. Distinct from check-mode (which converges nothing and arrives via the port's DryRun bit); a dry run already implies --diff.

vault.description: ansible-vault password source(s). The referenced CredentialRef MUST already be on the Step's credentialRefs — the existing use-grant check at dispatch stays the single authorization path (§2.5, ADR-0009/0052). No second credential channel is opened. v8 (ADR-0153 D4, closing ANS-011) accepts EITHER the v7 object (one identity) OR an ARRAY of entries, each with an optional `id`. One field with two shapes rather than a second field: a `vaultIds` alongside `vault` would be two declarations of one concept, and the moment both were set there would have to be a rule about which wins — the implicit precedence §2.4 refuses. Non-breaking by necessity rather than politeness: the registry keeps one live actuators/ansible.input and a Step cannot pin a version (ADR-0132 D4), so an array-only v8 would fail every shipped object-form Step the moment it landed.

credentialRef.description: Name of a CredentialRef on this Step, file-injected; the shim passes its path as --vault-password-file.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several.

id.description: Optional vault IDENTITY. With it the shim renders --vault-id <id>@<path>; without it, --vault-password-file <path> exactly as v7 did. Duplicate ids across entries are refused: two files claiming one identity is an ambiguity ansible resolves by ORDER, which is a silent winner by another name (§2.4).

credentialRef.description: Name of a CredentialRef on this Step, file-injected; the shim passes its path as --vault-password-file.

file.description: Optional filename within the CredentialRef's mount (/runner/credentials/<ref>/<file>). Omit when the ref injects exactly one file — the shim resolves it; required (and diagnosed, §1.8) when the ref injects several.

Duplicate ids across entries are refused: two files claiming one identity is an ambiguity ansible resolves by ORDER, which is a silent winner by another name (§2.4).

eeImage.description: DEPRECATED and IGNORED (ADR-0117 D3a). No runtime path reads it: executeJobPlugin builds JobSpec without an Image, so the dispatcher always uses the global EE. Per-Step EE selection is by Actuator declaration (ADR-0103) — a Step selects an Actuator whose declaration carries the image — which keeps the core content-blind instead of teaching it to read an ansible param. Retained so nothing breaks; removal booked once no writer emits it.

check.description: DEPRECATED and IGNORED (ADR-0117 D2). Check-mode has exactly one mechanism — the sovereign port's DryRun bit, which the shim maps to --check --diff (ADR-0051 MF6, superseding ADR-0019's params.check). Retained because the AWX materializer still writes it for imported check templates; deleting it before that writer is redirected to Step.DryRun would silently convert an imported check job into a converging apply (§1.8). Removal booked once no writer emits it.

allOf.$comment: ADR-0134 D4 — play (inline), scm (cloned) and playbook (mounted from the Actuator's contentDir) are the three content sources, and project/ has room for exactly one of them. Stated as three PAIRWISE refusals rather than one `not: {anyOf: […]}` so a validation failure names the offending pair instead of reporting that the whole document matched something it should not have (§1.8).
